hypothesis: A definable Japanese customer segment has frequent, material cross-merchant purchase or delivery friction.
key_unknown: Share of households with >=3 merchants and >=4 orders/month, and whether their friction is material after carrier/merchant notifications.
falsification_test: CLA-E002: if <20% of a deliberately heavy-buyer sample reports >=1 material unresolved post-purchase exception per month, H01 is contradicted for the wedge.
decision_implication: Multi-merchant use is common, but delivery-miss pain is falling; the only plausible material friction left is exceptions (returns, refunds, missing items), which is untested.

hypothesis: Current merchant apps, carrier notifications, email, wallets, and aggregators do not already solve it adequately.
key_unknown: Whether heavy multi-merchant users experience residual gaps that free tools miss.
decision_implication: Compare against carriers' LINE flows and in-platform agents, not a strawman.

hypothesis: SUB: Delivery visibility ('when will it arrive') is not adequately solved by free tools.
key_unknown: Coverage of phone-matched LINE notices for non-LINE users.
falsification_test: If diary participants report <1 missed/unknown delivery per month, confirmed.
decision_implication: Do not lead with tracking.

hypothesis: SUB: Post-purchase exceptions across merchants (returns windows, refund confirmation, missing/damaged items) are not adequately solved.
key_unknown: Frequency, severity and current workaround time for exceptions.
decision_implication: This is the only consumer wedge worth testing.

hypothesis: Enough users will grant the data access and transaction authority required.
status: CONTRADICTED (for transaction authority); UNRESOLVED (for data access)
key_unknown: Inbox-connection and forwarding conversion in Japan.
falsification_test: CLA-E004 permission A/B; Visa-type survey already contradicts spending authority.
decision_implication: Design for read-only, minimum-data, per-order approval; abandon autonomous purchasing.

hypothesis: SUB: Users will connect an inbox or set up forwarding.
key_unknown: Permission grant rate for forwarding vs OAuth.
falsification_test: CLA-E004: <25% grant in a recruited heavy-buyer sample = contradicted.
decision_implication: Model base assumes 40%.

hypothesis: SUB: Users will authorise an agent to spend on their behalf.
key_unknown: Whether bounded, per-order approval changes acceptance.
decision_implication: Keep humans in the purchase decision; checkout = handoff.

hypothesis: A startup can obtain sufficient permitted, durable merchant/carrier/payment access.
status: CONTRADICTED (for purchase execution, consumer order APIs and delivery changes); SUPPORTED only for read-only email ingestion and merchant handoff
key_unknown: Whether amazon.co.jp emails still carry item names; whether any marketplace would partner.
falsification_test: CLA-E001 (Amazon JP email check); CLA-E003 (partner conversations).
decision_implication: The reliable service boundary is read-only tracking from user-forwarded email plus merchant handoff.

hypothesis: SUB: Consumer order data across top marketplaces is accessible via a permitted API.
decision_implication: Email/user upload only.

hypothesis: SUB: Purchase execution across top marketplaces is permissible for an independent agent in Japan.
decision_implication: Watch, do not build.

hypothesis: SUB: A third party can change delivery instructions for consignees.
decision_implication: Hand off to carrier channels.

hypothesis: SUB: Read-only order ingestion from email is permissible and durable.
key_unknown: Amazon JP email content; non-Gmail coverage.
decision_implication: Feasible substrate, fragile at the largest merchant.

hypothesis: Agentic checkout produces meaningful incremental benefit over existing checkout.
key_unknown: Time/error saved at the checkout step for already-logged-in users.
decision_implication: Existing saved-payment/one-click flows leave little checkout friction; value sits in discovery, which incumbents own.

hypothesis: Tracking and checkout reinforce each other commercially.
key_unknown: Conversion from tracking users to handoff purchases.
decision_implication: Model tracking as standalone; do not count on cross-subsidy.

hypothesis: Japan-specific requirements create an advantage worth more than the associated complexity.
key_unknown: Whether cross-ecosystem points optimisation is a durable, valued capability.
decision_implication: Localisation is table stakes that incumbents already have.

hypothesis: Customers can be acquired and retained through a realistic channel.
falsification_test: CLA-E002 recruitment yield; CLA-E003 partner interest.
decision_implication: Paid acquisition is not viable at modelled contribution.

hypothesis: Contribution economics remain attractive after failures, support, incentives, and acquisition costs.
key_unknown: Handoff share, attributable share, paid conversion, human minutes.
decision_implication: Only the upside case or partner-paid B2B2C clears break-even.

hypothesis: The company can defend value against incumbents, fast followers, and disintermediation.
key_unknown: Any asset not reproducible by platforms.
decision_implication: No moat identified; incumbents control data and can cut access.

hypothesis: A specific recent change improves feasibility or demand.
key_unknown: Japan launch dates for agent payment/protocol rails.
decision_implication: Cheap extraction is real; access is tightening; protocol checkout not in Japan.

hypothesis: The result can be a durable independent company rather than a feature, low-margin service, or inaccessible platform dependency.
status: CONTRADICTED (venture-scale Japan consumer); UNRESOLVED (smaller business / B2B)
key_unknown: Whether a merchant/partner payer exists for post-purchase exception handling.
decision_implication: If anything, B2B/B2B2C is the more viable shape.
